content:
**The merge driver does not exist where the merge happens**

ADR-0017 made the durable log conflict-free by declaring merge=union in .gitattributes. That driver is a LOCAL git mechanism; the merge that lands work here is the forge's merge button, which does not apply it. So the guarantee held on every machine and failed at the only place that mattered: the first memory-capturing PR merged clean and every subsequent one conflicted, on the append-only log, resolved by hand, where a dropped record is indistinguishable from one never captured.

The fix is the LAYOUT, not a better driver: one record per file, records/<yyyy-mm>-<id>.jsonl, the content hash as the filename. Two different records are two different paths, and git merges distinct added paths without consulting any driver.

Measured as a controlled experiment ON THE FORGE, not locally — same two records, same day, merge=union declared in both arms: the month layout reported mergeable_state "dirty", the per-record layout reported "unstable" (mergeable, checks pending). Locally, driver-free: month file CONFLICT, one file each clean. The fragmentation objection ADR-0017 used to reject sharding did not survive pricing: reading the 2052-record store got FASTER (70ms vs 133ms; the 7MB split by newline dominates), packed size +15% once, per-append cost unchanged.

Three things worth carrying forward. (1) A test that green-lights a guarantee its production setting cannot honour is green for the wrong reason: records-merge.integration.test.mjs declared the union attribute in its own temp repo and so proved a property the merge site never had. (2) My first merge-tree probe reported the month layout merging clean WITHOUT the attribute, which would have contradicted the ticket; the cause was the probe (scratch files inside the repo, git add -A, two branches that never got their commit), and it was caught by inspecting the branch tips rather than trusting the exit code. (3) Applying the promote drafts to temp copies and reading the RESULT found two gaps reading the drafts had not: the ADR states the layout a second time in its Decision section, and both artefacts closed the anti-custom-driver passage by pointing at the built-in union driver as the friction-free alternative.
